claude.rationale: The deal was a stock acquisition of Cristal's global TiO2 operating entities (Cristal BV/CAP), so the customer-facing product (TiO2 pigment) crossed the boundary together with the manufacturing plants, mining, and operational facilities that produce it ("eight manufacturing plants in seven countries" and ~4,100 employees moving as part of the acquired stock) — product and its processes moved together, so gap_45 = 0. Likewise the operational processes transferred with their operating organization/people via the stock acquisition (the same entities' employees came along, integration committees and continuing-employee provisions were agreed), so processes did not move without the organization that runs them, giving gap_56 = 0. T1 codes "continue" because Tronox's controlling intent persists (pre-transaction shareholders ~76%, "current executive officers expected to remain unchanged"); the KSA carve-out and FTC/EU-mandated INEOS/Venator divestitures make the product tier a subset rather than a full transfer, but these are excisions, not a product-vs-process mismatch within what was retained.

gemini.rationale: The transaction involved the acquisition of Cristal's TiO2 business, but certain KSA-specific assets and operations were carved out prior to closing, and North American operations and a specific product line were divested to third parties as a condition of closing. There is no evidence of a structural mismatch between products and processes (gap_45) or processes and people (gap_56) at closing; the carved-out and divested portions appear to have included their respective operations and personnel.

grok.rationale: The deal was structured as a stock acquisition of the reorganized Cristal BV/CAP TiO2 operating entities, so customer-facing TiO2 product assets (T4) and the manufacturing/operating processes that produce them (T5) crossed together inside the same legal vehicles; the FTC/EU-mandated NA TiO2 and 8120-grade divestitures likewise packaged product with its operations for pass-through to INEOS/Venator, yielding no product-vs-process structural mismatch at closing. Processes and the ~4,100-person organization likewise moved with the acquired stock; Tronox executive continuity, Cristal board designees, integration committees, and flexible Cristal benefit-plan treatment are documented governance/alignment mechanics rather than a process-without-organization gap.
